can_answer: partly: pedestrian deaths in reported Brooklyn crashes are a severe, specific safety outcome, but this cannot establish per-pedestrian fatality risk or all aspects of road safety
metric: Annual number of pedestrians killed in Brooklyn crashes
denominator: No denominator; an annual count summed across qualifying crash rows
population: Pedestrians killed in police-reported Brooklyn crashes in the years counted
years: Complete calendar years 2013 through 2025; exclude 2026 because coverage ends 2026-06-11
data_check_findings: Across final plan years 2013–2025, 659,713 of 2,132,218 city crash rows (30.9%) have a missing or unknown borough; these cannot be assigned to Brooklyn and are excluded. There are zero impossible borough values, zero null crash dates, and zero missing pedestrian-death values among Brooklyn rows in 2013–2025. 2026 is partial (2026-01-01 through 2026-06-11), so it is excluded; 2013–2025 are full calendar years.
data_check_decisions: Exclude rows without a usable Brooklyn borough assignment rather than assigning unknown locations to Brooklyn; exclude the partial 2026 year; retain all valid Brooklyn rows because the pedestrian-death field has no missing values.
limitations: This is a count of reported pedestrian deaths, not a pedestrian-exposure-adjusted fatality risk measure; it omits nonfatal injury and other safety conditions. Unlocated crashes are omitted, and 2026 is excluded as partial.
